ambient.summary: Four soft colour blobs that drift and inflate with the low end
ambient.description: Four large, softly-blurred colour blobs drift across the frame. Bass slowly inflates them and mid energy nudges their saturation, so the motion reads as breathing rather than beating. Migrated from the built-in ambient style; declares no permissions and does no networking.

aurora.summary: Aurora veils over a starfield and mountain silhouette
aurora.description: Soft aurora curtains flow above a starfield sky and a mountain silhouette. Each curtain is tied to its own frequency band, so its shape bends with the music rather than only its brightness. Migrated from the built-in aurora style; no permissions, no network.

bars.summary: 64-band bar chart with decaying peak-hold markers
bars.description: A classic 64-band vertical bar chart, each bar carrying a peak-hold marker that falls away slowly after a transient. The most legible way to actually read a spectrum. Migrated from the built-in bars style; no permissions, no network.

cassette.summary: Tape deck with bass-driven reels and L/R VU meters
cassette.description: An animated cassette deck: reels spun by bass energy, a label carrying a frequency-bar VU strip, and left/right VU meters. Falls back to SIDE A and NOW PLAYING when no track or playback state is reported. Migrated from the built-in cassette style.

circular.summary: 96 radial spokes around a bass-reactive glowing disc
circular.description: Ninety-six spokes radiate from a central disc that glows and swells with bass. Read from a 96-bin spectrum, so every spoke maps to its own band. Migrated from the built-in circular style; no permissions, no network.

city.summary: Neon skyline whose windows light on their own frequency bin
city.description: A night-time skyline silhouette under a moon that pulses with bass. Each foreground building window lights when its assigned frequency bin does, so the city reads as an equaliser you can look at. Migrated from the built-in city style.

constellation.summary: Drifting particles that link to neighbours and scatter on kicks
constellation.description: Seventy particles drift around wandering home positions, drawing lines to nearby neighbours as they pass. A kick shockwaves them outward before the springs pull them back. Migrated from the built-in constellation style.

freqgrid.summary: Scrolling 32x16 grid of frequency rows over time
freqgrid.description: Sixteen frequency rows scroll across thirty-two columns of history, giving a compact picture of how the spectrum has moved over the last few seconds rather than only where it is now. Migrated from the built-in freqgrid style.

hud.summary: Fictional aircraft HUD driven by frequency bands and onsets
hud.description: Altitude and speed tapes, a compass ribbon, a pitch ladder and a bottom spectrum strip, all driven by frequency bands and onset detection. Entirely fictional instrumentation - it is a visualiser, not an instrument. Migrated from the built-in hud style.

kaleidoscope.summary: Twelve rotating spectrum-scaled diamonds in screen blend
kaleidoscope.description: Twelve diamonds rotate and scale from a twelve-bin spectrum read, blended with screen so overlaps brighten rather than occlude. Migrated from the built-in kaleidoscope style; no permissions, no network.

liquid.summary: Lava-lamp metaballs that swell and merge with bass
liquid.description: Fluid metaball blobs swell, drift and merge under bass energy, with mid-driven highlight ripples running across their surfaces. Migrated from the built-in liquid style; no permissions, no network.

minimal.summary: Three dots pulsing to bass, mid and treble
minimal.description: Three dots, one each for bass, mid and treble, sized by their band's energy. The quietest thing in the catalog and the one that survives being looked at all day. Migrated from the built-in minimal style.

neonbars.summary: 56 glowing mirrored bars with heavy bloom
neonbars.description: Fifty-six mirrored bars scaled from a fifty-six-bin spectrum, drawn with enough glow to read as neon tubing rather than a chart. Migrated from the built-in neonbars style; no permissions, no network.

orbital.summary: Stacked rotating rings and comets around a pulsing sun
orbital.description: Concentric rings rotate at different rates around a central sun that pulses with bass, each ring marked with frequency ticks and trailed by its own comet. Migrated from the built-in orbital style.

particles.summary: 140 spring-and-drag particles that scatter on bass spikes
particles.description: A hundred and forty particles held by springs to wandering home positions, scattered outward by bass spikes and dragged back between beats. Migrated from the built-in particles style; no permissions, no network.

perlin.summary: Glowing particles steered by a noise flow field
perlin.description: A pseudo-Perlin noise field steers a swarm of glowing particles, with bass driving both drift speed and particle size. Migrated from the built-in perlin style; no permissions, no network.

pixelled.summary: Retro 32x20 LED grid with an accent-to-red heat map
pixelled.description: A thirty-two by twenty LED matrix coloured per cell with a heat map running from accent through accent2 to red, driven by a thirty-two-bin spectrum. Migrated from the built-in pixelled style.

radial.summary: Slowly rotating ring of 96 mirrored spectrum spokes
radial.description: Ninety-six spokes mirrored around a slowly rotating circle, each scaled by its own spectrum bin. Migrated from the built-in radial style; no permissions, no network.

ribbon.summary: A single filled symmetric ribbon from a 48-bin spectrum
ribbon.description: One continuous symmetric ribbon, filled rather than stroked, shaped by a forty-eight-bin spectrum read. Migrated from the built-in ribbon style; no permissions, no network.

scope.summary: CRT-phosphor oscilloscope trace over a faint grid
scope.description: A phosphor-green oscilloscope trace rides a slow-moving carrier wave over a faint grid, its amplitude driven by the spectrum. Migrated from the built-in scope style; no permissions, no network.

spectrogram.summary: Scrolling waterfall heatmap of the spectrum over time
spectrogram.description: Every frame's sixty-four-bin spectrum becomes a new colour column, scrolled in from the right - a waterfall of what the music has been doing, not just what it is doing. Migrated from the built-in spectrogram style.

splitmirror.summary: 80 gradient bars mirrored around a glowing centre line
splitmirror.description: Eighty gradient bars mirrored above and below a glowing centre line, each scaled from an eighty-bin spectrum read. Migrated from the built-in splitmirror style; no permissions, no network.

starfield.summary: Bass-warped 3D starfield with a kick-pulse depth flash
starfield.description: Stars stream toward the viewer at a speed warped by bass, with a depth flash on every kick. Migrated from the built-in starfield style; no permissions, no network.

strings.summary: Physically-modelled strings plucked by onset detection
strings.description: Vibrating strings across a fretboard, physically modelled rather than drawn: each is plucked on kick, snare and hat onset edges and continuously excited by its own spectrum bin. The most simulation-driven visualiser in the catalog.

tunnel.summary: Six blurred waveform layers riding band energy
tunnel.description: Six layered waveform paths, each with its own blur, riding bass, mid and treble energy over a sixty-four-bin spectrum to read as depth. Migrated from the built-in tunnel style.

vinyl.summary: Spinning record with album art and a parking tonearm
vinyl.description: A turntable with the album art as its label, a kick-reactive glow ring, and a multi-piece SVG tonearm that swings in on play and parks when playback stops. Migrated from the built-in vinyl style.

waveform.summary: Gradient ribbon line biased toward the energetic low end
waveform.description: A gradient ribbon line weighted toward the low and mid end of the spectrum and blended with overall loudness, so quiet passages thin out rather than flatline. Migrated from the built-in waveform style.

tile-birds.summary: Recent bird sightings near you, from eBird
tile-birds.description: Lists recent bird observations within a radius you choose, using the eBird public API. Needs a free eBird API key and a latitude/longitude; declares net access to api.ebird.org and nothing else.

tile-dailychallenge.summary: Today's LeetCode daily problem, difficulty and acceptance
tile-dailychallenge.description: Shows LeetCode's daily coding challenge - title, difficulty and acceptance rate, with a link through to the problem. Uses the public activeDailyCodingChallengeQuestion query; declares net access to leetcode.com only.

tile-dictionary.summary: First definition of a word you choose, key-less
tile-dictionary.description: Looks up a word you configure in the Free Dictionary API and shows its first definition. Public and key-less; declares net access to api.dictionaryapi.dev only.

tile-githubprs.summary: Open pull requests waiting on your review
tile-githubprs.description: Lists open pull requests where your review has been requested, each linking through to GitHub. Needs a personal access token; declares net access to api.github.com and a stored github_pat secret.

tile-launches.summary: Upcoming rocket launches with provider and window
tile-launches.description: The next eight upcoming orbital launches with their status, provider and launch window, from The Space Devs' public launch library. Declares net access to ll.thespacedevs.com only.

tile-onthisday.summary: Historical events for a date you pick, from Wikipedia
tile-onthisday.description: Events that happened on a given month and day, from Wikimedia's On This Day feed, each linking to its article. Declares net access to api.wikimedia.org only.

tile-phonenotifs.summary: Latest push from an ntfy topic you own
tile-phonenotifs.description: Shows the most recent message on an ntfy.sh topic, which is a simple way to get phone notifications onto a second monitor. Needs the topic name as a stored secret; declares net access to ntfy.sh only.

tile-quote.summary: Today's quote and author, refreshed hourly
tile-quote.description: Fetches ZenQuotes' quote of the day every hour and shows it with its author. Public and key-less; declares net access to zenquotes.io only. Migrated from the built-in quote tile - same endpoint, same cadence.

tile-randomwiki.summary: A random Wikipedia article intro, refreshed hourly
tile-randomwiki.description: Pulls one random Wikipedia article each hour and shows its title and opening extract. Declares net access to en.wikipedia.org only.

tile-stocks.summary: One ticker's last price against its previous close
tile-stocks.description: Shows a single ticker's latest price with its previous close underneath, from Yahoo Finance's public chart endpoint. Declares net access to query1.finance.yahoo.com only.

shaderlab.summary: Shadertoy-compatible GLSL shaders with a 512x2 audio texture
shaderlab.description: A fragment-shader host speaking the standard Shadertoy contract: mainImage(), the standard uniforms, and iChannel0 as the classic 512x2 audio texture (FFT row, waveform row). Eight original audio-reactive shaders ship built in - click the surface to switch (left third goes back), and the choice persists. Shadertoy's site default licence is CC BY-NC-SA, so everything bundled here is original; the host exists so future visuals can be a text file instead of an engine. No permissions, no network.

beatgrid.summary: Cells, bars and palettes fire on Spotify's actual beat grid
beatgrid.description: Musically-synced rather than amplitude-reactive: with Spotify connected, cells flip on the track's analysed BEATS, the frame flashes on BARS, and the palette rotates per SECTION with brightness following each section's mastered loudness. Without a grid (no Spotify, or the analysis endpoint unavailable) it falls back honestly to live onset envelopes and says so in the corner tag. No permissions, no network of its own - the grid arrives through the host.

beatlab.summary: Onset strength, threshold and detected BPM as a lab strip
beatlab.description: The onset detector's own working view: onset strength scrolling against its threshold line with beat markers, a brightness trace, and the detected BPM in large type. As much a diagnostic as a visual - the number is measured, not guessed.

chroma.summary: The 12 pitch classes as a radial meter, naming the strongest
chroma.description: A radial meter over the 12 pitch classes with the strongest named in the center - watch it agree with the song's key. The chroma fold sums every octave of the spectrum into its pitch class, so chords light multiple segments.

console.summary: L/R meters, level history, and honest dB numbers
console.description: A mixing-console corner: L/R meters with peak-hold, a rolling 5-second level history, and live numbers - peak, RMS, crest factor, correlation - in real dB. Declares stereo; a mono source honestly reads correlation 1.00.

equalizer.description: The classic hi-fi front panel: 20 frequency bands, 24 segmented LEDs each, green through amber to red at the top, with falling peak-hold dots. Migrated from the built-in style; no permissions, no network.

moire.summary: Two ring systems drift with the bass and interfere
moire.description: Two concentric ring systems drift apart on bass energy and interfere, producing live moire patterns that shimmer with the music. Calm source, calm rings; a drop tears them apart.

notebars.summary: Three octaves of piano keys lit by the chroma fold
notebars.description: The spectrum folded onto three octaves of piano keys - black keys dimmed, the loudest pitch classes lighting their keys. Melodies walk visibly along the keyboard.

ridgeline.summary: Unknown Pleasures as a live scrolling spectrum
ridgeline.description: Each tick pushes a new mirrored spectrum line onto a stack of receding ridgelines - the Unknown Pleasures album cover as a live display. History reads top to bottom.

silk.summary: One continuous ribbon tracing a bass-driven epicycloid
silk.description: A single continuous ribbon traces an epicycloid whose radii breathe with the bass, thickening on energy and fading into its own trail. Slow music draws lace; loud music scribbles.

terrain.summary: Spectrum history as a wireframe range receding into distance
terrain.description: The spectrum extrudes a wireframe mountain range that recedes into the distance - each frame is a new front ridge, history rolls away behind it. Louder music builds taller terrain.

vectorscope.summary: Mid/side stereo point cloud with correlation and width
vectorscope.description: The stereo field as engineers see it: a mid/side point cloud - tall is mono, wide is spacious - with live correlation and width meters. Declares stereo; a mono source correctly collapses to a vertical line at correlation 1.00.
